subject: accepted-state primitive

selection.proposedPrimitive: PROPOSED concrete Agent-specific one-shot accepted-policy store backed by AtomicReference<AcceptedPolicyEnvelope>
selection.proposedPrimitiveBeforeCorrection: single-shot expected-base accepted-policy state store described through the generic S01AcceptedPolicyStore<S>
selection.genericFormIsNotTheProductionPrimitive: S01AcceptedPolicyStore<S> is spike scaffolding retained for the mechanism proofs and the benchmarks. An arbitrary S may be mutable, so it is explicitly NOT the production contract.

productionContract.store: final class AcceptedPolicyStateStore with exactly one field: final AtomicReference<AcceptedPolicyEnvelope> current
productionContract.envelope: record AcceptedPolicyEnvelope(String runtimeInstanceId, long acceptedSequence, EffectiveTracingPolicy policy)
productionContract.policy: record EffectiveTracingPolicy with exactly eight Category A leaves and no Category B state
productionContract.read: current() returns the published immutable envelope reference
productionContract.write: commit performs exactly one expected-base compareAndSet

selection.memoryVisibilityMechanism: one final AtomicReference holding one immutable all-final-field envelope; get() is a volatile read, compareAndSet is a volatile write; successful commit happens-before every subsequent observing read
selection.hotPathMechanism: single AtomicReference.get() followed by plain final-field reads; zero allocation, zero lock, zero JMX
selection.placementRationale: platform-tracing-otel is on the Spring application classpath (platform-tracing-spring-boot-autoconfigure/build.gradle:9). The extension module's absence from the application classpath is already asserted by root build.gradle:472 and gradle/c3-published-consumer/build.gradle:44,46, making Agent-classloader exclusivity structurally enforced.

proofs.requirement: N concurrent writers on one expected base yield exactly one APPLIED and N-1 STALE; acceptedSequence advances by exactly 1; final state is the winner's; no lost update
proofs.observed: 250 rounds x 8 writers; 1 APPLIED and 7 STALE every round; sequence +1 every round; 2000 attempts produced 250 accepted commits; final sequence 250

proofs.requirement: the store performs no retry, rebase or merge
proofs.observed: candidate constructions 2000 = one per attempt; sequence advances +1 per round rather than +8; commit accepts a built candidate rather than a builder function, so there is nothing the store could re-invoke

proofs.requirement: expected runtimeInstanceId != actual -> STALE, state unchanged, sequence unchanged
proofs.observed: STALE returned; accepted envelope identical by reference afterwards, proving no compare-and-set occurred; sequence and policy unchanged

proofs.requirement: expected acceptedSequence != actual -> STALE, state unchanged
proofs.observed: both stale-behind and stale-ahead bases return STALE with the accepted envelope identical by reference

proofs.requirement: semantically identical policy digest -> store CAS not invoked, acceptedSequence unchanged
proofs.observed: UNCHANGED returned; accepted envelope identical by reference; sequence unchanged. REJECTED and FAILED likewise never enter the store. No spy or seam needed: a successful commit always installs a new envelope instance, so reference identity is a direct no-CAS observable.

proofs.requirement: after a successful commit, readers see fully constructed immutable state with no partial or mixed fields and no reader-side synchronisation
proofs.observed: 20000 commits with 6 unsynchronised reader threads; readers verified policy self-consistency and acceptedSequence == policy.seed() on every observation; 0 violations

proofs.requirement: hot-path read allocates zero bytes, takes no lock, constructs no wrapper

jmh.profileCaveat: documented in platform-tracing-bench/build.gradle as indicative on a developer host; gc.alloc.rate.norm is counter-derived and sound at this profile, ns/op is feasibility evidence only

results.note: includes construction of a fresh candidate policy record and its one-entry immutable map on every call

jmh.groupAggregateNote: readWhileCommit group gc.alloc.rate.norm = 1.021 B/op is the GROUP aggregate, amortising the writer's two allocations per commit across all eight threads' operations. It is not reader allocation.

proofs.requirement: manual sequence increment, unconditional set, in-place mutation, runtimeInstanceId bypass, rebase and diagnostics in the CAS payload are impossible or require breaking encapsulation
proofs.observed: surface is exactly {current, commit}; no set/put/replace/reset/update/getAndSet/force method; no method accepts an envelope; no void-returning method on the envelope and all its fields are final; expected-base components are exactly (runtimeInstanceId, acceptedSequence) with null identity rejected; CAS payload components are exactly (runtimeInstanceId, acceptedSequence, policy); consecutive reads return the same instance so there is no copy-on-read; the store declares exactly one field and it is a final AtomicReference

proofs.requirement: determine executably whether the existing generic primitive satisfies E3
proofs.observed: no tryUpdate overload accepts an expected base and all return boolean, so STALE is inexpressible; in a deterministic latch-controlled handoff the builder was invoked twice with bases [0, 1], the stale caller was told it succeeded rather than STALE, and the stale caller's value overwrote the winner; with 8 writers on one logical base all 8 reported success and the version advanced +8 where E3 requires 1 and +1

deepImmutabilityContract.mapCopyOfRejected: Map.copyOf does not specify iteration order, so it does not establish deterministic ordering. The semantic requirement is an immutable key-sorted representation, of which Collections.unmodifiableNavigableMap(new TreeMap<>(input)) is one satisfying form; the exact implementation remains P1 work.
